The October 16 09:00 UTC through October 17 09:00 UTC reporting window contains 26 commits and seven merged PRs in daily-logger. The work spans article correction and review records, durable feedback controls, action reconciliation and deployment-build repairs. Most merges landed Friday, October 16; the review-UI merge landed early Saturday, October 17. Together they make the daily review loop easier to inspect, preserve editorial work during interruptions and keep action history traceable. The remaining qualifications are recorded below.

## What shipped

### daily-logger ([#370](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/370))

PR [#370](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/370) (merged October 17 06:22Z) made article review cycles legible across reviewers and revision rounds. The UI now groups reviews by article version, distinguishes the claimed `reviewer.name`/`reviewer.sessionId` identity from the authenticated GitHub `pullRequest.author`, preserves or deliberately clears feedback across interruptions, and refreshes stationary PR/commit previews when their data arrives late. Seven focused browser journeys and 413 native tests pass on the hosted CI run. Production is live at [log.jim.software](https://log.jim.software). Vercel preview builds and public-page checks passed; live authenticated editorial behavior on those previews remains unverified because the recorded GitHub OAuth callback was rejected. ([#370](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/370))

## The decisions

### Reviewer identity is the claimed name in review data, not the authenticated GitHub carrier — *model-behavior-as-design*

The UI now explicitly distinguishes who the review record says reviewed the article — the claimed `reviewer.name` and `reviewer.sessionId` embedded in the review JSON — from the authenticated GitHub carrier (`pullRequest.author` when the review is linked through a PR). In the data model, these are separate paths: `reviewer.name`/`reviewer.sessionId` carry the claimed identity (a model name or editor handle from the review JSON) and `pullRequest.author` carries the GitHub-authenticated account when present. Presentation ambiguity arose when Codex sessions and human editors touched the same review record: the component now explicitly labels reviewer/session claims separately from the authenticated GitHub carrier. Separating them makes multi-reviewer and human-plus-model cycles legible, and gives future identity types (a third reviewer, an audit agent) a clear place to live without touching either existing path. When no PR link is available, the component explicitly displays “GitHub submission account not linked to this record.” It does not infer a submitting account from the reviewer claim.

Tags: `editorial-pipeline`, `provenance`, `model-behavior-as-design`

### Feedback selection survives interruption via keyed storage, selective pruning, and deliberate clear — *model-behavior-as-design*

Rather than always preserving selected feedback across interrupted requests or always discarding it, the component keys saved drafts by actor, date, and article blob. On reload or reconnection, selections whose source findings are unavailable are retained (the absence of evidence is not treated as evidence that a finding is ineligible); selections whose source findings are present but no longer current or open are pruned. While a request is in flight, pruning is skipped — the component does not discard selections during an uncertain send. The editor can deliberately clear retained selections when a request is not being sent and selections exist; the control is disabled during a send or when there is nothing to clear. Editable feedback is preserved. This is a model-behavior-as-design decision — the system's behavior during failure is itself the UX, not a secondary concern. The tested paths cover reload-after-save, in-flight retention, and deliberate clear; broader timeout/navigation guarantees beyond those tested paths are not claimed.

Tags: `model-behavior-as-design`, `hardening`, `editorial-pipeline`

### Automatic discovery of eligible review PRs complements explicit proposal registration — *assistant-centric*

Before #368, the article UI could surface explicitly registered pinned proposals at their open-PR heads, but could not automatically discover eligible same-repository review-data PRs. #368 adds automatic bounded discovery, validating four things server-side before returning findings: (1) the PR's immutable head SHA, confirming the tip hasn't moved; (2) the changed-file boundary, confirming the PR touches only expected review-data paths; (3) the registry manifest, confirming the review record is well-formed and registered; (4) the source article blob, confirming it matches the article the review claims to cover. During discovery, head, changed-file, manifest and blob-validation failures are disclosed as unavailable data and prevent new writes. Write-time stale-selection and moved-target checks can separately reject a submission; those responses are distinct from the discovery GET projection. Stale or incomplete history also disables writes explicitly. #368 also adds persistent correspondence, making the review surface a durable pre-merge tool rather than ephemeral browser state. Review registration and article acceptance remain distinct operations.

Tags: `assistant-centric`, `provenance`, `ci-cd`

### Section discussion is durable via GitHub as the correspondence store — *security-as-emergent-ux*

Discussion threaded against article sections was previously ephemeral browser state — it vanished on reload. #368 replaced that with GitHub as the backing store. Saved discussion envelopes carry date, visible article blob, requestId, threadId, actor, and a nullable section label. Reload restores all fields. GitHub was chosen over a separate database or localStorage because it keeps correspondence auditable, co-located with the PR review record, and requires no new infrastructure. On GitHub API unavailability, failed refresh preserves prior receipts as last observed and disables new writes until recovery; proposal discovery failures are reported as unavailable entries with disabled writes. These failure behaviors are covered by controlled ready/outage/recovery tests. Proposal-discovery GET availability and write-time rejection/conflict responses are distinct failure paths. Production rate-limit resilience and broader availability guarantees beyond these tested controls are unknown.

Tags: `provenance`, `assistant-centric`, `editorial-pipeline`

### Action queue identity is strictly preserved across reconciliation — no re-paraphrasing — *tooling-for-iteration*

#373's reconciliation treated original action descriptions, IDs, and completion objects as immutable. Three missing October 15 suggestions were restored and three October 16 records were resolved without touching any other row's identity. PR #373 delivers admission checks that throw before API publication and a continuous check conserving all baseline identities plus historic completion objects — covered identity drift is made visible by those controls rather than passing silently. The verified post-reconciliation baseline is 85 open / 125 completed. The current generated queue has since grown to 88 open / 125 completed after three new suggestions were admitted; those three new IDs are intact and not settled merely because this article is corrected. Whether the open-action count is a healthy working backlog or a growing graveyard requires week-over-week queue-growth data not available in this report.

Tags: `provenance`, `ci-cd`, `editorial-pipeline`

## Roadmap pulse

**Open PRs**

Green builds and a source-year check alone do not grant readiness or merge authority. It is one of the follow-ups associated with issue #357. Draft-to-ready promotion and merge remain conditional on owner decision.

**lego-village-pipeline #44** [DRAFT, DO NOT MERGE] — Analysis-only draft; no implementation authority. A distinct bounded design artifact with its own review gates.

The three lego-village-pipeline drafts are distinct bounded design artifacts with their respective review, import, and owner gates. They do not require disposition from this article cycle.

**Issue #357 pilot status**

The registered pilot covers October 13–16 at the source revision used for this report. The October 15 accepted-source record and October 16 PRs #369/#371 document completed correction-and-verification cycles; this report does not label the next one a first or second cycle. Issue [#357](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/issues/357) already gives observable completion criteria: an authorized editor and agent can identify the relevant source-bound review, request a correction without implicit acceptance, see stale/proposed/published states and inspect the dogfood evidence. Those observations do not qualify the always-on runner or adjudicate historical findings. Today's proposed review in #377 extends the dated review record; article acceptance and review publication retain their own receipts.

Comments add producer/runtime and trace obligations. GitHub adapter/producer identity and optional credential research are separate from the accepted Dolt/handoff inspector. Whether an owner session is scheduled is unknown from available records; the issue does not require provisioning accounts before the accepted existing-source inspector or unrelated article work can proceed.

**Skill telemetry**

The collector distinguishes the legacy skill-telemetry stream frozen since May 12 from its primary skill-dispositions ledger and exports selected-source and freshness fields. The reviewed follow-up directions are the authorized article cycle and the existing #372 review. Each retains its own owner and evidence conditions; this report establishes no new dependency ordering between them.

The following block retains the original generator suggestions verbatim so their identities and history survive. Their reviewed dispositions immediately below govern how they should be read.
